Versus
 Rajesh Pandey

Appearance:
 Shri Eshaan Datt - Advocate for the appellant.
None for the respondent.

Order
Per: Justice Anuradha Shukla

This first appeal has been filed by the appellant/wife, assailing the judgment and decree dated 22-12-2016, passed by the Principal Judge, Family Court, Katni, in RCS HM 66A/16, whereby the divorce petition filed by the respondent/ husband on the ground of desertion was allowed.
2 .
Admittedly, the parties were married on 1-5-2004 and lived together till 7-11-2015, with no child born out of this wedlock.

The divorce petition earlier filed by the husband, with case number 34A/2005, was dismissed on 25-1-2007, and even the first NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:50437 2 FA-60-2017 appeal preferred by the husband before the High Court, with FA No.152/2007, was dismissed on 20-4-2011.
It is also admitted that thereafter a petition under Section 9 of Hindu Marriage Act with case number 124A/15 was filed by the husband, but that was withdrawn on 12-2-2016.

3. The divorce petition in brief was that the behavior of wife was very discourteous and insulting towards the elder family members of husband; she was not the least interested in performing household tasks; husband was therefore, compelled to file the divorce petition, but his petition and also the first appeal both were dismissed by Courts.
He thereafter filed a petition for restitution of conjugal rights but during mediation proceedings, wife refused to resume marital relationship,

sentences.text: This second divorce petition was filed on the grounds that parties are living separately for last 10 years and no marital relationship was established between them during this period.
It was claimed that wife has withdrawn from the company of husband without any reasonable cause and therefore, husband has no other option but to request for a decree of divorce.

4 . The appellant/wife contested the divorce petition by claiming NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:50437 3 FA-60-2017 that in the light of dismissal of earlier divorce petition and also the first appeal, the second divorce petition is not maintainable.

It was also submitted that wife was forced to leave the matrimonial house and in these circumstances a maintenance of Rs.4000/-
was allowed in her favor.
Respondent/ husband was not interested in marital relationship since the inception and therefore, he denied to make appellant/wife as nominee in his service record.
He preferred the first divorce petition within a period of one year from marriage.
Wife was always keen for restoration of marital relationship and therefore, did not file any police case under section 498A of IPC.
A request was therefore made to dismiss the divorce petition.
5 . The trial Court, based on the pleadings of the parties, settled the issues, recorded the statements and passed the impugned judgment.

6 . The appellant/wife is assailing the impugned judgment on the grounds that it is illegal, improper and incorrect as it has failed to appreciate the evidence in correct perspective and ignored the judgments passed in first divorce case and the first appeal arising out of that case.

It is submitted that trial Court mechanically interpreted the ground of cruelty and accepted the evidence of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50437 4 FA-60-2017 husband which was full of omissions, contradiction and improvements.
It was ignored that the wife was subjected to cruelty and humiliation on account of demand of dowry and was compelled to live in her parental house.

The malafide intentions of husband were revealed when he refused to nominate wife in his service record, in utter disregard of the fact that wife was not having any source of income to maintain herself.
A request has therefore been made in this appeal to quash the impugned judgment and dismiss the divorce petition.
7 . Learned counsel for the appellant/wife has been heard on merits while the respondent remained absent and has thus been proceeded ex-parte.
8. The facts which were not contested before the trial Court were that the parties were married in the year 2004 and they are living separately since 7-11-2005.
The earlier divorce petition registered as RCSHM 34A/2005 was filed on the ground of cruelty and desertion and both of these grounds were not found proved by the concerned trial Court.
The first appeal No.152/2007
against that dismissal
was not considered on merits and it was dismissed on 20-4-2011 on account of non-payment of litigation expenses and maintenance amount.

It is also not in dispute that subsequent to NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50437 5 FA-60-2017 dismissal of that first appeal, a petition under section 9 was filed by the respondent husband but after the session of mediation, he requested for withdrawal of petition regarding which order dated 12-2-2016 was passed marked as Exhibit P/2.

2 9.

sentences.text: The order sheet of civil suit 124A/2011 registered on the basis of petition of section 9 Hindu Marriage Act reflects that appellant/wife had filed a written statement and issues were framed by the trial Court.
The settlement of issues signifies the fact that wife was opposing the petition of restitution of conjugal rights and her contesting written statement compelled the Court to settle issues.
Thus, the submission made by the learned counsel for the appellant/wife can not be accepted on its face value that she was always keen for restitution of conjugal rights.

10. The grievance of wife is that dismissal of petition as withdrawn revealed the malafide intentions of husband that he was never willing to resume married life with wife and this petition of section 9 Hindu Marriage Act was filed with a dishonest objective.

However, this submission is not acceptable having considered that respondent husband was a low-grade employee who could not have afforded expensive litigation cost just for the sake of deceit or vanity.

Even assuming that respondent husband NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50437 6 FA-60-2017 was not keen in re-establishing the marital ties, there is no explanation why the appellant/wife was opposing the petition of section 9 Hindu Marriage Act and also why she did not file any such petition on her own accord.

11. The written statement submitted by the wife before the trial Court claims that husband does not want to cohabit with her but the entire pleadings are silent about the circumstances in which she left her matrimonial house.

The judgment of Ex.P/1 in RCSHM No.34A/05 reveals that appellant/wife left the matrimonial house on 7-11-2005 when her father came along with two policemen of Police Station Madhavnagar, and she accompanied them to her parental house.
This finding reflects that respondent husband had not consented for wife to leave the matrimonial house, but father of wife and two policemen took her along with them against the wish of husband.

This judgment also confirms that respondent/husband never went to the parental house to bring her back, but this resentful attitude on the part of husband does not burden him with any guilt in the wrong of desertion committed by the wife.

It appears to be the plain and simple choice of wife to leave the matrimonial house in the company of her father and two policemen and it is also reflected that NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50437 7 FA-60-2017 subsequently she made no attempts to come back to the matrimonial house which she left willingly.

12. Wife has the complaint that husband never came to her parental house to bring her back to the matrimonial house, but it appears to be a case of inflated ego, where husband was not keen to bring her back as she left the house against his consent and more so with the assistance of police personnel, while wife herself was not ready to take initiative on her own to go back to her matrimonial house, which she left willingly and against her husband's wish.

Instead of visiting the parental house of wife, husband chose to file the petition of Section 9 of Hindu Marriage Act, which we have already discussed in earlier para.
13. Section 9 of Hindu Marriage Act, places the burden of proof on the person withdrawing from the company of other spouse to establish that there was any reasonable or just cause for this withdrawal.
Here we can observe that no such reasonable cause has been established by the appellant/wife.
She is claiming that she was being harassed for dowry demand, but no police report or complaint was made by her in this regard.

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the appellant husband has placed heavy reliance on the fact that a maintenance order was passed in NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50437 8 FA-60-2017 favour of appellant/wife reflecting that she was living separately on for a reasonable cause.

To consider this argument, firstly, order passed under Section 125 Cr.P.C has not been placed on record by appellant/wife and secondly, in the order passed under section 127 Cr.P.C and placed on record as Ex.D/7, the only consideration before the Court concerned was whether an enhancement in maintenance amount would be justified or not.
Therefore, no information can be extracted from Ex.D/7 about the reasonableness of the cause for living separately.
Accordingly it is held that wife has failed to justify the circumstances of living separately and deserting the husband since 2005.
15. The earlier divorce petition was filed after the permanent separation of parties in the year 2005 and parties did not live together thereafter.
The earlier divorce petition was contested on various grounds, but bad habit of taking liquor by husband was not a part thereof.

Although in the written statement filed before the trial Court in this second divorce case, the allegations of taking liquor was not made by wife against the husband, but strangely, in her Court testimony in paragraph 7, she has made allegation about said addiction of husband.
It is not explained how and when she came to know about this addiction of respondent.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50437 9 FA-60-2017

Making unfounded baseless allegation is also an aspect of cruelty which cannot be ignored and the only inference that can be drawn in the circumstances of the case is that the appellant/wife by not restricting to her limited pleadings and making unsubstantiated serious allegations against her husband, she was clearly taking steps towards dissolution of marriage.

16. In the case of V. Bhagat v. D. Bhagat, (1994) 1 SCC 337 , the Apex Court expressed the view that in spite of making various allegations against the husband, if the wife still claims to live with him,
the obvious conclusion would be that she has resolved to make the life of husband more miserable and dissolution of marriage is the best solution in such circumstances.

entities.text: V. Bhagat v. D. Bhagat, (1994) 1 SCC 337
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 17. Based on the foregoing discussion, we do not find any ground to interfere in the findings of the trial Court and accordingly, this appeal is dismissed and the decree of the divorce passed by trial Court is upheld.
